exposure: American Society of Anesthesia (ASA) score greater than 3
length of hospital stay after surgery
cohort: The study included 1173 patients who underwent surgical procedures in the Obstetric and Gynecology department of a teaching hospital in rural India between September 2010 and February 2013.
finding: The incidence of surgical site infections was 7.84%, with obstetric surgeries having a significantly lower incidence (1.2%) compared to gynecological surgeries (10.3%), and multiple patient and procedural factors were identified as independent risk factors for SSI.
mod_finding: Obstetric surgeries were associated with a lower incidence of surgical site infections (1.2%) compared to gynecological surgeries (10.3%).
